_doc: Inflation benchmarks for retrospective editions dated in 2011: the target for the current calendar year as publicly known at each cutoff. End-2010 state of the verified 2010 register, plus the 2011 current-year targets set earlier (Türkiye 5.5%, Brazil 4.5%, Colombia 3%, Indonesia 5%) and the value changes announced during 2011 (China's annual objective; the RBI's end-of-fiscal-year WPI projection, taken from its quarterly reviews only, as in 2010). Each new source URL was fetched and its claim checked; sources are shown only once published. Wording-only updates without a value change (FOMC projections, UK Budget, Canada's target renewal) are not recorded.
note: Three economies had no headline-CPI target: the Federal Reserve had no numerical target (2.0% is an analytical benchmark), the RBI's objectives referred to the wholesale price index (the benchmark is the RBI's stated end-of-fiscal-year WPI projection), and the Bank of Thailand targeted core inflation. Benchmarks apply to the headline CPI series used here. Each benchmark is the target for the current calendar year as publicly known at the cutoff; China's is the government's annual CPI objective, announced each March (until then the previous year's applies). Where a range was set, its midpoint is used; for the euro area's ‘below but close to 2%’, 1.9%. Sources are listed only if published on or before the edition’s last eligible day.

US.wording: No numerical inflation target. FOMC projections released 23 Nov 2010: 'projections of this mandate-consistent rate of inflation exhibited a central tendency of 1.6 to 2.0 percent, little changed from June' (PCE). 2.0% headline CPI is this monitor's analytical benchmark.
US.index: PCE price index (FOMC projections); benchmark applied to headline CPI

urls.label: FOMC Summary of Economic Projections, 2–3 Nov 2010 meeting (released 23 Nov 2010)

XM.wording: 'A year-on-year increase in the HICP for the euro area of below 2%' … 'maintain inflation rates close to 2% over the medium term' (below but close to 2%: 1.9% used).

urls.label: ECB press release, evaluation of the monetary policy strategy, 8 May 2003

JP.wording: 'Understanding of medium- to long-term price stability', reviewed April 2010: it 'falls in a positive range of 2 percent or lower, and the midpoints of most Policy Board members' understanding are around 1 percent'.

urls.label: BoJ, Outlook for Economic Activity and Prices, April 2010 (30 Apr 2010)

GB.wording: June Budget 2010: 'the independent Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Bank of England will continue to target 2 per cent inflation, as measured by the 12-month increase in the Consumer Prices Index (CPI)'.

urls.label: HM Treasury, Budget 2010 (June, HC 61), 22 Jun 2010, para 1.27

CA.wording: Inflation as measured by the CPI at 2 per cent, with a control range of 1 to 3 per cent (renewed November 2006 for five years).

urls.label: Bank of Canada, Renewal of the Inflation-Control Target: Background Information, Nov 2006

AU.wording: Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 30 Sep 2010: 'keeping consumer price inflation between 2 and 3 per cent, on average, over the cycle' (midpoint 2.5%).

urls.label: RBA Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 30 Sep 2010

CH.wording: The SNB 'regards prices as stable when the national consumer price index (CPI) rises by less than 2% per annum' (midpoint of 0–2%: 1.0%).

urls.label: SNB Quarterly Bulletin 4/2007, 'Inflation forecasting as part of the monetary policy concept'

SE.wording: 'The annual change in the consumer price index (CPI) is to be two per cent', tolerance band ±1 percentage point.

Riksbank Monetary Policy Report 2008:1, February 2008

NO.wording: 'Annual consumer price inflation of approximately 2.5% over time.'

urls.label: Norges Bank Monetary Policy Report 3/07

NZ.wording: Amended Policy Targets Agreement (signed 18 Dec 2008): target unchanged, 'keep future CPI inflation outcomes between 1 per cent and 3 per cent on average over the medium term'; the only change adds a statement of the government's economic objectives.

urls.label: Minister of Finance press release, 'Amended Policy Targets Agreement Signed', 19 Dec 2008 (Scoop)

Report on the Work of the Government (2010), full text (Xinhua, NPC site)

IN.index: WPI (new series); benchmark applied to the CPI series used here

TR.wording: End-2011 CPI inflation target of 5.5%, set jointly with the Government in 2009 as part of the three-year point-target path (6.5% for 2010, 5.5% for 2011) and restated in the CBRT's policy document of 10 Dec 2009.

PL.wording: Continuous CPI target of 2.5% with a symmetric ±1 percentage-point band, restated in the Monetary Policy Council's monetary policy guidelines (resolution of 30 Sep 2009, published 14 Oct 2009).

urls.label: Monitor Polski No. 66, item 868: MPC resolution of 30 Sep 2009 on monetary policy guidelines (published 14 Oct 2009)

HU.wording: 'An inflation rate near the 3 per cent medium term objective.'

MNB Quarterly Report on Inflation, February 2008

CZ.wording: 'The CNB announces the new inflation target as annual consumer price index growth of 2% (with a tolerance band of ± 1%), effective from January 2010'.

KR.wording: Medium-term target of 3.0% ±1.0 percentage point for 2010–12, set by the Monetary Policy Committee on 26 Nov 2009: the BoK widened its inflation target range 'to 2 to 4 percent from the existing 2.5 percent to 3.5 percent … the median inflation target remains intact at 3 percent'.

CL.wording: 'Keep annual CPI inflation around 3% most of the time, within a tolerance range of plus or minus one percentage point.'

CO.wording: Target for 2011 set by the Board on 19 Nov 2010: 'definió la meta de inflación de 2011 en un rango entre 2% y 4%, con 3% como meta puntual para efectos legales'.

TH.wording: Core inflation target of 0.5–3.0% (quarterly average), in force since the Cabinet decision of 1 Sep 2009 (midpoint 1.75%).
